To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the upper bound on MH depends on the top mass Mt only through the combination Mt2 − Mt1, (ii) the two-loop correction is negative and relatively small (≲ 3%) with respect to the leading order result, (iii) the upper bound is not affected by the choice of tan β, and (iv) for the infrared fixed point scenario, we have MH < 90 GeV for Mt < 180 GeV.
the upper limit on the Higgs mass is 140 GeV (86 GeV) for Mt = 190 GeV (170 GeV) and Ms ⩽1 TeV, and that this limit is not sensitive to further details of the model.

the two-loop corrections to the upper bound on MH are negative and relatively small, that the upper bound on Mh is a function of Ms, Xt and tanβ, that it does not depend on further model details, that the upper bounds are significantly lower than the ones obtained by using the one-loop result, that the upper limits are significantly lower than those obtained using the one-loop results and that the upper limits on MH are lower than the ones found by using the one loop result.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether or not a Higgs boson with mass in the range 100 GeV < MH < 140 GeV can be produced at the LHC.
the computation of the upper limit on the mass of a Higgs boson.
the question whether or not the lightest HIGGS boson can be found at LEP2 or the Tevatron.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for Mt ⩾ 170 GeV, the lightest Higg boson mass in a supersymmetric model is bounded from above by the experimental value of Mt, and that the lightest Higss boson mass is bounded from above, for any Mt, by the experimental value Mt = 175 GeV.

, for Mt ⩾ 170 GeV, a Higgs boson with mass below 140 GeV would be an unambiguous signal for supersymmetry, with the lower bound decreasing for smaller values of Mt and/or Ms, and increasing for larger values of Xt and/or tan β.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the upper bound on MH is 140 GeV in the most general case and 90 GeV in the infrared fixed point case.
in the Minimal Supper-symmetric Standard Model the upper bound on MH is not significantly modified by the two-loop corrections.
the lightest Higg boson mass is not bounded to lie above 140 GeV in the MSSM, as long as the supersymmetric threshold corrections are included.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lightest Hiss boson mass in supersymmetric models is not a problem.
the two-loop corrections to the Higgs mass are negative and small.
the lightest Hiss boson mass can be as light as 140 GeV, even in the presence of large radiative corrections.
